subject.title: Google Chat: markdown renders as raw text; typing indicator says 'OpenClaw is typing' instead of app name

question: Should Google Chat translate assistant Markdown into Google Chat-supported markup, strip unsupported Markdown to plain text, or keep the current markdown-capable behavior and only fix the identity.name typing fallback?
rationale: Current source declares Google Chat markdown-capable and Google's docs support a limited Markdown dialect, but automation should not choose the permanent channel rendering contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Convert Supported Markup
options.body: Implement a Google Chat renderer that maps common assistant Markdown into Google Chat-supported syntax, degrades unsupported constructs, and fixes the typing identity fallback.

options.title: Plain Text Policy
options.body: Treat Google Chat as plain text, strip Markdown before delivery, and update metadata, docs, and tests to remove the current markdown-capable contract.

options.title: Typing Fix Only
options.body: Land only the identity.name fallback and document that Google Chat currently receives markdown-capable text without full dialect conversion.

recommendation.title: Convert Supported Markup
recommendation.body: Implement a Google Chat renderer that maps common assistant Markdown into Google Chat-supported syntax, degrades unsupported constructs, and fixes the typing identity fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: He has strong Google Chat polish/refactor history and is the best available routing candidate for the rendering-policy choice.
